results.title: Move GPU lab default region for reserved-capacity pricing
results.author: tvasquez-rh

answer:
This is not a capacity shortage, and waiting will not fix it.

**What the job shows.** Job 4172093 launched its GPU workers in `ca-west-1` and failed with `Unsupported: Your requested instance type (g6e.12xlarge) is not supported in your requested Availability Zone (ca-west-1a)`. Unsupported means the zone does not offer that type at all -- it is a different error from InsufficientInstanceCapacity, and the "no On-Demand Capacity Reservation" line earlier in the log is only a warning.

**Where the region comes from.** The item, `rhoai-gpu-labs/llm-finetune-workbench/prod.yaml` in rhpds/agnosticv, sets `worker_instance_type: g6e.12xlarge` but does not set `aws_region` at all, so it inherits the account-level default from `rhoai-gpu-labs/account.yaml`, which agnosticv merges into every catalog item under that account.

**Which change.** PR **#20417** ("Move GPU lab default region for reserved-capacity pricing", merged 2026-09-29) changed only `rhoai-gpu-labs/account.yaml` (plus docs), moving the account default region to ca-west-1. That lands between the last good provision (2026-09-26) and the failures. The item's own last PR, #19862 (a notebook image bump on 2026-08-11), is unrelated.

**Fix.** Pin `aws_region` (e.g. us-east-1) in the workbench's own config, or pick a GPU instance type ca-west-1 offers; and check the other GPU items under rhoai-gpu-labs, which inherited the same region.

**Category:** configuration. **Confidence:** high.
